data.title: Thingino: Open-Source Firmware for IP Cameras
data.author: zakki
data.article_summary: 这篇文章列出了各种支持Thingino固件的IP摄像头型号及其硬件细节，包括SoC、图像传感器、Wi-Fi模块和闪存芯片大小。由于制造商可能在不通知的情况下更改硬件，因此这些参数必须匹配才能获得支持。文章详细列出了室内、灯泡形和室外IP摄像头的具体型号和硬件配置，例如360 AP1PA3、AJCloud T-CP2011-W32A、Eufy C120、Wyze Cam Pan 2等。还提供了安装指导链接和相关资源，如GitHub仓库、Discord服务器和Telegram群组。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenIPC和thingino开源固件的应用及相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• 一些用户如[cnst]和[tmjwid]对thingino固件表示支持，强调了其在老旧摄像头上的易用性和性能提升。例如，[tmjwid]提到其在Wyze摄像头上的升级过程顺利，并赞赏了其夜视功能的改进。
• [glonq]和[1024core]则关注其对特定品牌摄像头（如Yi和Wyze）的支持情况及实际应用效果，尤其是对广告和应用兼容性的不满。
• [Roark66]指出该项目缺乏基本的AI运动检测和警报功能，认为这是其不足之处。
• [zakki]和[2bluesc]提供了技术细节和资源链接，帮助其他用户更好地理解和使用thingino固件。
• [rcarmo]则关注到HomeKit支持的缺失，并提到其之前使用ESP32摄像头的经验。
• [aag01]作为开发贡献者之一，分享了其组合使用多种工具构建家庭监控系统的经验，并表示对thingino的支持。

补充讨论：
• [harel]表示对该项目的存在感到高兴，并分享了成功修复旧摄像头的个人经验。
• [lammylamy]提到在尝试刷机过程中遇到的问题，如Wyze2摄像头变砖。
• [zakki]在最后提出了对开源自托管视频录制和处理工具的推荐需求。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在功能上的不足，特别是AI运动检测和应用兼容性（如HomeKit支持）方面。
• 用户对广告干扰的不满和开源固件带来的实际改进形成对比。

总体来看，讨论围绕thingino固件的技术实现、实际应用效果及功能扩展的可能性展开，既有正面支持的声音，也有对其不足之处的批评和建议。

data.title: 3D Line Drawings
data.author: tansh
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何通过增强3D高斯溅射（3D Gaussian Splatting）技术生成3D线条图。作者Amritansh Kwatra描述了利用Chan等人的方法，将照片转换为传达几何和语义信息的线条图，并结合3D高斯溅射生成实时辐射场渲染。具体方法是将原始图像替换为根据Chan等人的模型生成的线条图，然后进行3D高斯溅射处理。这一过程可以在两个阶段进行：在结构自运动（SfM）计算相机姿态和稀疏点之前，或在训练3D高斯溅射之前。最终生成的3D线条图根据视角变化，类似于传统素描效果，且保留了一定的颜色信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某项创意作品的评价与技术讨论

不同观点：
• 赞赏与赞美：
  - 多位评论者对作品表达了直接的赞赏和惊叹。他们称赞作品的创意和执行，比如[yodon]、[anastasiaess]、[trizoza]和[carl_bot]。
  - [wombatpm]将作品与过去的技术（Quake NPR）联系起来，表达了对作品的认可。

• 技术性讨论：
  - [vessenes]详细描述了作品的技术实现方式，强调了实验性和创造性，并对当前技术的发展感到振奋。
  - [kkoncevicius]对作品的互动功能（缩放和旋转）感到惊讶，但承认对技术细节不太理解。

• 技术争议：
  - [kookamamie]对作品的复杂性提出了疑问，建议是否可以通过单目深度估计等更简便的方法实现。

• 具体应用讨论：
  - [edg5000]讨论了3D高斯溅射技术在不同场景中的潜在应用，特别是无人机摄影测量，显示出对该技术未来发展的关注。

补充讨论：
• 文化参考：
  - [abrookewood]将作品与《Borderlands》游戏的艺术风格联系起来，提供了一个文化参照点。

• 幽默与期待：
  - [nathan_douglas]以幽默的方式提到《Return of the Obra-Dinn》续作，暗示了对类似风格作品的期待。

争议的焦点：
• 技术实现的复杂性与简便性：[kookamamie]对技术复杂性提出质疑，认为可能有更简便的方法。

44792441.article_content:
Creating 3D Line Drawings
Amritansh Kwatra
June 30th, 2025
This is an experiment examing how to create a 3D line drawing of a scene. In this post, I will describe how this can be done by augmenting the process of generating
3D Gaussian Splats
3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
, by Kerbl et al.
and leveraging a process to transform photographs into
Informative Line Drawings
Learning to Generate Line Drawings that Convey Geometry and Semantics
, by Chan, Isola & Durand
.
Examples
The majority of scenes shown above are generated using a
contour
style.
You can switch the active scene using the menu in the top-right corner of the iframe
. Each scene is trained for 21,000 iterations on an Nvidia RTX 4080S, using
gaussian-splatting-cuda
from MrNerf with default settings. Examples here were generated using scenes from the
Tanks & Temples Benchmark
. The scene is interactive, and rendered using
Mark Kellogg's web-based renderer
.
To explore these scenes in fullscreen,
click here.
How it works
Creating Line Drawings from Images
⊕
Figure 1.
(a)
A source image from the Caterpillar scene in
Tanks & Temples
.
(b)
A generated line drawing in the
contour
style.
(c)
A generated line drawing in the
anime
style.
Images are transformed into line drawings using the approach introduced by Chan et al. in
Learning to Generate Line Drawings that Convey Geometry and Semantics
. They describe a process for transforming photographs into line drawings that preserve the semantics and geometry captured in the photograph while rendering the image in an artistic style. They do this by training a generative adversarial network (GAN) that minimizes
geometry
The geometry loss is computed using monocular depth estimation.
,
semantics
The semantics loss is computed using CLIP embeddings.
, and
appearance
The appearance loss is based on a collection of unpaired style references.
losses. Their work is fantastic and I recommend reading their paper if you're interested in the details. Figure 1 depicts the input photograph and output line drawing in two styles, generated using Chan et al.'s
code and model weights
.
3D Gaussian Splatting
3D Gaussian Splatting is a technique that transforms collections of
posed images
Images for which we estimate the relative position and rotation of the camera in the scene. Usually, this is computed using Structure-from-Motion (SfM).
into a volumetric representation called a radiance field. Generally, scenes can be created from collections of images captured from multiple overlapping viewpoints, either by taking multiple photographs from different angles or by sampling an input video while moving through the scene. For more complete details on 3D Gaussian Splatting, I encourage you to read
the paper
or watch this
explanation video
from Computerphile.
The scenes that are produced using 3D Gaussian Splatting are photorealistic and can be rendered at real-time rates using existing tools such as WebGL. However, I noticed that if the images used to train the 3D Gaussian Splat were swapped out with the
line-drawing counterparts
While I transformed the images into line drawings, this transformation could be carried out using a number of other stylistic effects.
then the resulting scene would depict a kind of 3D line drawing. Similar to
regular sketching
Illustrating a 3D scene as a 2D drawing from a specific perspective.
, the lines that are rendered are view-dependant and change based on your perspective in the scene.
Swapping Source Images
⊕
Figure 2.
The transformed images can be used to create 3D line drawings by swapping them for the original images in one of two places, shown here in green. Either before using SfM to generate the sparse model and camera poses or prior to training the 3D Gaussian Splat. The former computes SfM points based on the transformed images, while the latter keeps the points from the original images and computes the rendering loss using the transformed images. Figure adapted from the
original 3D Gaussian Splatting paper
.
Generating these 3D line drawings requires only a slight modification to the conventional process for generating 3D Gaussian Splats. At a high level, we simply swap the original images with the ones generated using Chan et al.'s method for transforming images into informative line drawings. This swap can happen in two places: prior to training the 3D Gaussian Splat or prior to estimating camera poses and sparse points using structure-from-motion (SfM).
When images are transformed prior to training the 3D Gaussian Splat, the camera poses and initial 3D Gaussians are derived from the original images but the loss is computed by comparing the rasterization output to the informative line drawing. As a result, the final scene also captures slight amounts of color that is not present in the transformed images. I believe this is a side-effect of intializing the 3D Gaussians using the original images. If you transform the images prior to applying SfM, the ini

data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 德克萨斯农工大学开发的CLARKE系统利用无人机影像和人工智能，在几分钟内快速评估飓风和洪水后的损害情况。该系统由计算机科学与工程博士生Tom Manzini和救援机器人专家Robin Murphy博士领导开发，可以在短短七分钟内评估2000户住宅的损毁情况，帮助应急响应人员迅速制定救援计划。CLARKE使用先进的计算机视觉和机器学习算法，生成详细的损害报告和绕行路线，特别适用于农村或难以到达的地区。该系统已经过超过21,000栋房屋的训练，并在2024年飓风季成功部署于佛罗里达和宾夕法尼亚。其快速评估能力显著加速了救灾响应，被视为改变游戏规则的工具。

Science & Tech
AI Turns Drone Footage Into Disaster Response Maps In Minutes
A system developed at Texas A&M uses drone imagery and artificial intelligence to rapidly assess damage after hurricanes and floods, offering life-saving insights in minutes.
Jul 28, 2025
By
Lesley Henton
,
Texas A&M University Division of Marketing and Communications
4 min. read
CLARKE was trained on drone images from over 21,000 houses across 10 major disasters.
Credit: Texas A&M University College of Engineering
A tool developed at Texas A&M University is set to transform how emergency responders assess damage after disasters. The technology, known as CLARKE (Computer vision and Learning for Analysis of Roads and Key Edifices) uses artificial intelligence and drone imagery to evaluate damage to buildings, roads and other infrastructure in a matter of minutes.
CLARKE was created by a team of researchers led by Tom Manzini, a Ph.D. candidate in computer science and engineering, and
Dr. Robin Murphy
, a pioneer in the field of rescue robotics.
“This is the first AI system that can classify building and road damage from drone imagery at this scale and speed,” Murphy said. “We’re talking about assessing a neighborhood of 2,000 homes in just seven minutes. That kind of speed can save lives and resources.”
The system has already proven its value during the 2024 hurricane season, when it was deployed in Florida and Pennsylvania following Hurricanes Debby and Helene.
The Magic Of Machine Learning
The name CLARKE is a nod to science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke’s quote: “Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic.” According to Murphy, the name was inspired by drone pilots working with the system who began calling its machine-learning capabilities “magic.”
But there’s nothing mystical about the science behind it. CLARKE uses cutting-edge computer vision and machine-learning algorithms to analyze drone footage, overlay damage assessments on maps, and generate spreadsheets listing each structure’s address and damage level. For roadways, it even includes a Google Maps-style route planner that helps responders avoid impassable roads.
CLARKE doesn’t just tell you what’s damaged, it tells you how to get around that damage. That’s critical when every second counts.
Dr. Robin Murphy
Senior Professor of Computer Science and Engineering
Texas A&M University College of Engineering
In rural or hard-to-reach areas, traditional damage assessments can take days, delaying aid and complicating logistics. With CLARKE, officials could launch drones and receive a comprehensive damage report within minutes, dramatically accelerating response times.
“Rural counties often have lost wireless connectivity so they can’t send imagery to state and federal agencies for manual inspection,” Murphy said. “CLARKE empowers them to take immediate action.”
The system was trained on drone images from over 21,000 houses across 10 major disasters, including Hurricanes Harvey and Ian. This extensive dataset allows CLARKE to recognize a wide range of damage patterns, making it adaptable to different types of disasters, including hurricanes, floods and wildfires.
Training The Front Lines
While the technology itself is groundbreaking, its success depends on the people using it. Last month, more than 60 emergency responders from 38 agencies and eight private companies gathered in Tallahassee, Florida, for a two-hour awareness training session on CLARKE. The event, hosted by Florida State University, was expected to draw 15 to 20 participants but ended up with nearly 100 registrations, highlighting the growing interest in AI-driven disaster tools.
David Merrick, program director of the Emergency Management and Homeland Security Program at Florida State University and task force lead for unmanned aerial systems for the state of Florida, praised the system’s capabilities.
“This is a game changer for rural counties — they can fly drones and then immediately understand the extent of damage in their area rather than wait days for the information from other sources,” Merrick said. “It will help make damage assessment more efficient and effective.”
An image from CLARKE, which can assess damage on 2,000 homes in seven minutes.
Credit: Texas A&M University College of Engineering
Looking Ahead
CLARKE’s development began in 2022, and its creators continue to refine the system based on real-world feedback. After its deployment in 2024, the Texas A&M team participated in a tabletop exercise hosted by the AI Institute for Societal Decision-Making at the Florida Office of Emergency Management in April 2025 to gather input from responders. That session not only generated valuable suggestions but also sparked demand for formal training, leading to the June event in Florida.
Murphy sees a bright future for CLARKE, both as a practical tool and as a platform for further research.

data.title: As a linguist, I want to find the words to measure chronic illness
data.author: Avshalom
data.article_summary: 文章由语言学家M Corvi撰写，描述了慢性疾病患者在寻求诊断和表达病痛时的困境。作者讲述了自己在多次求医后，虽然进行了各种测试，但始终缺乏明确的诊断或语言来描述自己的症状，如 mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS) 和 postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS)。作者指出，医学常依赖可观察的现象，但对如疼痛或不适等主观感受缺乏准确的描述和测量方法。作者强调，患者和医生需合作寻找或发明适当的词汇来表达这些“看不见”的感受，并认为定性描述应先于定量测量，以全面了解疾病。文章呼吁对“无形”疾病如长新冠（Long COVID）进行更深入的理解和研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：慢性疼痛及功能障碍的描述与测量

不同观点：
• GarnetFloride：强调慢性疼痛与急性疼痛在体验和描述上的不同。慢性疼痛需要围绕疼痛来调整生活，类似于与配偶的关系。疼痛的程度难以用简单的数字衡量，且个体差异显著。举例说明不同情况下疼痛的感知差异，并指出患者希望被相信的诉求。

• rpaddock：分享了因妻子因慢性疼痛自杀而成为倡导者的个人经历，特别提到了颅内低压和氟喹诺酮类抗生素中毒的问题。引入了“勺子理论”来描述慢性病患者的日常活动限制，并建议通过消除饮食中的茄科植物来改善症状。

• PaulKeeble：讨论了用于量化长新冠和慢性疲劳综合症（ME/CFS）功能障碍的Funcap问卷。指出目前测量工具的不足，并强调ME/CFS疲劳的独特性和难以传达性。提出目前尚无被广泛接受的生物标志物。

• user568439：描述了妻子长新冠经历中遇到的医生不重视问题，包括医生不愿进行进一步测试和缺乏对症状触发因素的理解。强调了患者在寻求帮助时遇到的挫折和医生缺乏好奇心和帮助意愿的问题。

• vpribish：认为文章通过个人故事传达了人类代价和内部体验描述的困难。指出当前1-10评分系统的局限性，并提出系统问题的复杂性，包括恶意行为者和 incompetence 的存在。认为改进工具并不一定是明显的“胜利”。

• stared：指出语言的虚拟性与体验的真实性，认为需要更好的方法来命名和测量内部体验。提出利用大型语言模型（LLMs）将个人记录转化为摘要，从而实现更准确的测量。

• captainbland：认为证据比词语更重要，指出慢性条件的症状本身就是证据。提出目标-结果差距的概念，用于解释患者的实际情况，并讨论了在工作和社会中被视为负担的问题。建议可能需要一个新术语如“supportphobia”来描述避免支持的行为。

• onecommentman：提到疑病症（hypochondria）可能影响5%-10%的人口，并指出这可能是医疗成本上升的一个驱动因素。引用了心理学文章来支持这一观点。

• francisofascii：指出不仅是慢性病，任何病毒性疾病都难以描述和找到可靠的生物标志物。患者感觉“不适”、“不活力”，但医疗专业人员可能无法准确判断。

• resource_waste：建议教授维特根斯坦的《逻辑哲学论》和威廉·詹姆斯的实用主义，以帮助理解语言的基础性和科学的有限性。认为这种教育可能有助于培养医生的谦逊和公众的解决方案导向。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多种慢性疼痛和疾病的描述工具和理论，如“勺子理论”和Funcap问卷。
• 强调了语言和测量工具在传达和理解内部体验方面的局限性。
• 提出了医疗系统中存在的医生缺乏好奇心和帮助意愿的问题。
• 指出了社会对科学现实主义的信仰与科学实际能力之间的差距。

44771569.article_content:
Commentary
As a linguist, I want to find the words to measure chronic illness
Written by
M Corvi
–
August 1, 2025
Heather Hogan / The Sick Times
Let me paint a scene that is all too familiar: I’m not feeling well (again), I go to the doctor (again), they take some blood (again; I turn my head away) and poke at me in whatever way my insurance company deems appropriate.
The result is a long sheet of seemingly arbitrary numbers that indicate
something
about my metabolic processes and the resulting sensations, and I leave without much information aside from some variation of: “These tests tell me that your body seems to be functioning the way everyone else’s is. So we leave you linguistically empty-handed, without a diagnosis or words for these sensations. In conclusion, you’re fine.”
Then why do I feel like I’m full of noodles and static electricity? Where’s the electric noodle test, Doc?
If you also have a complex chronic illness, you’re probably familiar with this experience. These conditions and diseases create a massive linguistic gap that can be difficult for patients to bridge — and even more difficult for medical providers because they don’t experience what we do every day in our bodies.
So what words can I, a linguist and a patient with sensations perceivable only to me, use to fully capture these
mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS
) and
postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS)
sensations to my providers?
And, more generally,
how can we measure
our unsettling internal realities if we can’t even name them? How do you effectively measure something like pain, cognitive dysfunction, or feelings of noodliness when so much of medical measurement is reliant on readily observable phenomena — or, stuff that usually has really precise words?
In these moments when I am overwhelmed by this gap, I remind myself that
immaterial to others
doesn’t mean
unreal
— and that, after all, people have words to explain immaterial concepts like gods and quantum physics. The words for these unseeable sensations in my body must exist
somewhere
, and it’s up to patients and healthcare providers to work together to either find or invent them.

My body has always been quick to reject the world. With a family full of medical anomalies, I knew I would one day get my own diagnoses. Growing up, I had seen women in my family suffer from things that were readily dismissed by both clinicians and the general public — namely, chronic pain, fibromyalgia, and migraines. There was never a doubt in my mind that these illnesses caused suffering in the bodies of the people I cared about, even if I couldn’t see or feel the sensations that characterize them.
Eventually, many of these sensations would manifest in my own body. They are bizarre, uncomfortable, and painful sensations that I frequently struggle to find the words for.
I suspected I had MCAS in spring 2019. I began to react strangely to food I’d enjoyed my entire life, had sudden bouts of unexplainable hives, and was often dizzy. To advocate for myself with doctors, I consulted the much-hated “Dr. Google” (that’s
Dr. Google Scholar
to you!). I read any peer-reviewed paper with the right keywords, Wikipedia’d the hell out of any biology I didn’t know, frequented message board after message board, and eventually cobbled together a list of the appropriate tests for my symptoms.
I knew something was wrong with me, and I was determined to articulate it into numerical existence. I eventually did get my diagnosis in March 2022 — which is, comparatively speaking, a very short timeline for receiving a diagnosis of MCAS. I was diagnosed with POTS a few months later after going through a similar gauntlet.
I knew something was wrong with me, and I was determined to articulate it into numerical existence.
Over the course of my diagnoses and ongoing treatment, I’ve internalized a few things about language, illness, and measurement. The first is that, even though it gets easier over time, how I describe the sensations in my body will always be inadequate. That’s not a reflection of me — language can express only so much, and I can’t AirDrop my sensations to another human to make them feel exactly what I’m feeling.
Second, my doctors and I can’t just take a yardstick or thermometer to sensations like pain or discomfort to measure them. data.title: Build Your Own Lisp
data.author: lemonberry
data.article_summary: 《Build Your Own Lisp》是一本教你使用C语言创建自己的编程语言的书。全书通过1000行代码，引导读者学习C语言并开发一个类似Lisp的语言。书中探讨了Lisp的独特之处，帮助读者提高实际项目开发能力和问题解决技巧，同时写出优雅的代码。该书提供免费在线阅读，也可购买印刷版或电子书以获得更好的阅读体验。许多读者表示，实现自己的Lisp让他们感到成为更完整的C程序员，并认为每个程序员都应尝试这类项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕构建Lisp和学习C语言的讨论，涉及教程质量、适用性、现代C语言特性学习以及Lisp的扩展性。

不同观点：
• **关于教程的实用性和范围**：
  - [potato-peeler] 认为该书使用C99标准，询问是否有教程能教授C语言的新特性及避免标准库中的陷阱（如`gets`或`scanf`），并提到现代C语言与更新语言一样安全的观点，但缺乏相关书籍或教程。
  - [lskfiep] 认为该书不仅是“构建自己的Lisp”教程，更是一个学习C语言的好资源，尤其是在构建自己的编程语言方面，而不仅仅是Lisp相关。
  - [atan2] 引用一个网站将该书列入“应避免的内容”，暗示对该书质量的质疑。

• **对构建Lisp的看法**：
  - [gorgoiler] 对创建复杂项目（如Iosevka字体）的人表示钦佩，认为这些项目非常鼓舞人心，并激励自己努力。
  - [cardanome] 警告不要构建自己的Lisp，除非只是为了学习基础知识，因为某些方法长期来看可能不利于扩展。
  - [staplung] 提到Peter Norvig的一个用Python构建简化Scheme解释器的项目，作为学习Lisp构建的另一种选择。

• **对Lisp和C语言的学习建议**：
  - [dang] 提供多个相关讨论链接，显示该话题在不同时间点的讨论热度。
  - [tnlogy] 提到自己曾做过类似的编译器项目，并提到《SICP》这本书，询问其是否仍在课程中使用。
  - [coderatlarge] 对作者免费提供资源表示感谢，并分享自己的项目经验，强调错误处理和测试的重要性。

• **Lisp的扩展性和应用场景**：
  - [nyrikki] 提到曾使用包含在C中的纯Lisp学习语言，认为即使是简短的代码也能有效学习。
  - [codr7] 分享自己从不同角度解决问题的项目链接。
  - [adz5a] 询问是否有资源比较不同Lisp的表达能力、限制和特殊形式，并提到Lisp在LLM（大语言模型）中的潜在应用。
  - [golly_ned] 询问是否有使用现代C++构建Lisp的教程。

• **对历史人物的评价**：
  - [ale] 认为在构建和编译编程语言的教程中，使用Grace Hopper的肖像比Ada Lovelace更合适。

补充讨论：
• **关于教程深度和语言实用性**：
  - [dark-star] 认为大多数教程在涉及尾调用优化、延续、CPS和`call/cc`等高级主题时停止，使得构建的语言仅为玩具语言，但同时也肯定完成整个过程的价值。

争议焦点：
• 该书的质量和适用性：一些人认为它是学习C和构建Lisp的优秀资源，而另一些人则质疑其长期适用性和深度。
• 构建Lisp的实际价值：有人认为这些教程仅能构建玩具语言，而其他人则认为即使是玩具语言也有其学习价值。

总结：评论中围绕“构建自己的Lisp”教程展开了多方面的讨论，包括其作为C语言学习工具的有效性、对现代C语言特性的覆盖程度、Lisp的扩展性以及在实际应用中的潜力。

data.title: A Carnival Attraction That Saved Premature Babies (2016)
data.author: pr337h4m
data.article_summary: Martin Couney was a renowned figure who ran infant incubator exhibits for over 30 years, most famously at Coney Island. His displays of premature babies in incubators drew large crowds, with an exhibit at the 1933-1934 Chicago World’s Fair being particularly successful. Couney, alongside pediatrician Dr. Julius Hess, cared for premature babies using advanced incubators, despite controversy over the ethics of displaying the infants. Couney claimed to have studied medicine in Europe, but evidence suggests he never officially qualified as a doctor. Despite this, his work saved thousands of babies and influenced American neonatal medicine, eventually gaining recognition as pioneering, though his lack of formal medical credentials remained a point of contention. His collaboration with Hess marked a significant step in gaining legitimacy in the medical field.

44770215.article_content:
Martin Couney holds up Beth Allen, a premature baby who was on view at the Coney Island attraction.
Beth Allen
Nurses in starched white uniforms and doctors in medical coats tended to babies in glass and steel incubators. The infants had been born many weeks premature and well below a healthy birth weight. Stores didn’t make clothes small enough to fit their tiny, skeletal frames so the nurses dressed them in dolls’ clothes and knitted bonnets.
A sign above the entrance read “Living Babies in Incubators” in letters so large they could be read from the other end of the Chicago World’s Fair grounds, which took place over 18 months in 1933 and 1934. The infant incubator exhibit was built at a cost of $75,000 (worth $1.4 million today) and was painted in a patriotic red, white and blue.
The men in charge were leading Chicago pediatrician Dr. Julius Hess and Martin Couney, who was known across America as “the incubator doctor.” Couney was a lugubrious man in his 60s, with thinning gray hair, a mustache and a stoop, something he jokingly attributed to a lifetime of bending over babies. Couney and Hess employed a team of six nurses and two wet nurses.
Martin Couney had run infant incubator exhibits, in which premature babies were displayed to the public, for more than three decades, most famously at Coney Island in New York City. He had long been regarded by desperate parents as a savior, one who offered medical help to babies written off as “weaklings” by mainstream medicine.
But for Hess, who was accustomed to carrying out his work in a more conventional hospital setting, this was a career first.
Miracle at Coney Island: How a Sideshow Doctor Saved Thousands of Babies and Transformed American Medicine (Kindle Single)
More about this product
The exhibit was a hit with the Chicago public who paid 25 cents and flocked by the hundreds of thousands to see the babies.
To celebrate the success of their facility, Couney organized a “Homecoming” celebration on July 25, 1934, for babies who had “graduated” from the incubators at the Chicago’s World’s Fair the previous summer. Of the 58 babies Couney and Hess had cared for in 1933, 41 returned with their mothers for the reunion. The event was broadcast live on local radio and across the fairgrounds.
On the radio program, Couney’s exhibit was portrayed by the announcer not as a frivolous sideshow spectacle, but as an invaluable medical facility:
The Incubator station for premature babies…is not primarily a place of exhibiting tiny infants. Instead, it is actually a lifesaving station, where prematurely born babies are brought from leading hospitals all over the city, for the care and attention that are afforded. The place is spick and span, with doctors and graduate nurses in constant attendance...
Because of the sideshow setting in which he operated, Couney’s career had always been controversial. Many in the medical professional viewed the “incubator doctor” with suspicion, others with outright hostility. The New York Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children had repeatedly accused Couney of exploiting the babies and endangering their lives by putting them on show.
None of the complaints was sustained, and by the 1930s, Couney was finally being taken seriously as a medical pioneer. Couney’s professional collaboration with Hess marked a key stage in his habilitation.
But while doing research for my radio documentary
Life Under Glass
, which is being broadcast on NPR stations around the country this August, and my book,
Miracle at Coney Island
, I made an incredible discovery about a man who has a claim to have changed the course of American neonatal medicine.
Couney never actually qualified as a medical doctor.
Throughout his career, Couney said he had studied medicine in Leipzig and Berlin. However, I could find no evidence of Couney (or Cohn/Cohen as he was known then) having studied medicine at a university in either city. To become a physician in Germany, one was required to write a thesis. The U.S. National Library of Medicine has copies of the German records: the librarians could not locate a thesis written by Couney.
Couney was deliberately evasive about his date and place of birth. I have discovered that he immigrated to the US in 1888 at 19 years old. But someone of that age would not be old enough to have studied at university in Leipzig and Berlin before going on to do graduate work in Paris at the knee of Pierre Budin, the father of European neonatal medicine, as Couney claimed to have done in numerous press interviews.
In the 1910 U.S. census, Couney listed his career as, “surgical instruments.” Though Couney claimed to be the inventor of an incubator, I have been unable to find any evidence that he registered an incubator patent in the U.S. More likely Couney was a technician. Yet by 1930 he was describing himself in the census as a “physician.”

• matsemann没有直接讨论执照问题，而是通过讲述祖父的幽默故事，暗示一些看似荒唐或非传统的做法并不一定有害，尽管这些做法并非严格遵循常规。
• alsetmusic通过引用历史实例（"Infantorium"），指出在历史上一些看似奇怪的实践（如展示早产儿）也曾被社会接受，并强调这种现象在当时并非孤例，以此暗示判断实践方式的标准会随时间变化。
• delichon引用了《国王的演讲》中的例子，认为有些非传统或自学成才的从业者也能具备出色的能力，并对此表示鼓励。
• Aardwolf关注具体操作中的实际问题（如如何正确匹配婴儿和父母），质疑在实际操作中可能存在的管理问题，但没有直接评价实践方式的合法性或道德性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应拘泥于传统资格认证（如执照），还是更应看重实际结果和贡献。LinuxAmbulance明确反对过度关注过程，而其他评论者通过实例和个人故事间接支持这一观点。
• 历史实例（alsetmusic提供的"Infantorium"）为讨论提供了一个独特的视角，强调社会对专业实践的接受度会随时间变化。
• 自学成才的例子（LinuxAmbulance和delichon）为讨论增加了对传统教育和资格认证的反思，认为非传统背景的人也能做出重要贡献。
• Aardwolf的评论提醒讨论中需要考虑的具体操作问题，如管理复杂性，这在实际应用中同样重要。

data.title: Apache ECharts 6
data.author: makepanic
data.article_summary:
Apache ECharts 6.0 发布了12项重大升级，旨在提升数据可视化的专业性和灵活性。主要改进围绕三个核心维度：

1. **更专业的视觉表现**：
   - 全新默认主题，现代设计语言。
   - 动态主题切换，无需重新初始化图表。
   - 支持暗黑模式，自动适配系统主题。

2. **扩展数据表达边界**：
   - 新增和弦图、蜂群图、散点抖动、断轴等新图表和功能，处理复杂数据场景。
   - 增强股票交易图表，提升标签能力和开箱即用的图表类型。

3. **释放组合自由**：
   - 新的矩阵坐标系，支持像表格一样组合图表和组件。
   - 增强的自定义系列，支持npm发布和动态注册。
   - 新增小提琴图、轮廓图等自定义图表。
   - 优化轴标签布局，防止重叠。

这些升级使ECharts 6.0在数据可视化方面更加强大、可靠和灵活，帮助开发者创造出更具创意的视觉作品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ECharts库的优缺点及其在不同场景中的应用

不同观点：
• homebrewer：赞赏ECharts的向后兼容性，特别是从其他库（如react-router）迁移过来的体验。其项目从5.6版升级到6.0版仅用了15分钟，且只有图例位置的改变，通过导入旧主题轻松还原。从商业库转到ECharts后没有后悔。
• dev_l1x_be：强调ECharts作为全面的图表解决方案，可以通过特定方法减少包大小，提供了一个链接说明如何操作。
• rorylaitila：认为ECharts总体最佳，快速、完整、易于上手，且具有良好的示例和渲染支持。但抱怨不同图表类型需要不同的数据结构，尤其是数据表功能不够完善和文档不全。
• derkades：对新版本发布感到兴奋，但觉得LLM（大语言模型）相关的描述难以阅读。
• ggregoire：长期使用ECharts，认为其功能齐全，且不像D3那样复杂。特别提到ECharts与React的良好兼容性，其他库往往缺少一些必要的功能（如多Y轴支持）。
• RyanHamilton：三年前评估多个图表框架后选择了ECharts，用于实时数据库可视化，效果极佳，仅有一个未实现的关键功能，现已修复。
• elric：特别喜欢新的和弦图，认为其工具提示和清晰渐变效果出色。
• kakadu：认为ECharts功能不错，但在扩展功能时遇到困难，例如实现甘特图需要深入源码。还提到翻译不够好。
• kylecordes：对ECharts高度赞赏，认为其功能丰富，商业替代品相形见绌。
• porridgeraisin：比较多个前端图表库后，认为ECharts和uPlot最好。最终选择ECharts是因为其动画支持和易用性，特别是与Vue的良好集成。

补充讨论：
• tnolet：询问是否有人从Highcharts切换到ECharts的体验。
• nirav72：询问是否有人使用ECharts进行实时数据的可视化。
• billfruit：询问ECharts是否支持交互式3D图表。

争议焦点：
• 不同用户对ECharts数据结构的复杂性存在争议，尤其是rorylaitila和kakadu提到的图表数据结构不一致和文档不完善问题，与其他用户对ECharts的高度赞赏形成对比。

总的来说，ECharts因其功能全面、易用性和向后兼容性受到广泛好评，但在文档和特定功能的实现上仍有改进空间。

44794926.article_content:
Apache ECharts 6 New Features
Twelve years ago, ECharts was first released on GitHub, planting the seed for an open-source journey.
From a simple charting tool to a visualization powerhouse supporting millions of developers; from a single front-end charting library to a comprehensive technology system covering mobile, large screens, and server-side rendering—over these 12 years, we've witnessed ECharts' continuous technical breakthroughs and have been delighted to see developers worldwide create countless stunning data stories with ECharts.
Now, Apache ECharts 6.0 is officially released, bringing 12 major upgrades to take your data visualization to the next level.
Feature Overview
Twelve years of accumulation, all for more ultimate visual expression. The core strength of Apache ECharts has always come from a deep understanding of developers' real challenges. When defining the direction for 6.0, the question was clear:
How can we make complex data presentation both powerful and elegant?
This drove us to evolve deeply around three core dimensions:
More professional visual presentation
: From a meticulously crafted default theme to intelligent dark mode switching, ensuring charts have a professional look and seamlessly integrate into modern applications.
Expanding the boundaries of data expression
: New chart types and features to handle complex scenarios and enable intuitive expression of deep data.
Unleashing freedom of composition
: From the revolutionary matrix coordinate system to reusable custom series and optimized axis labels—empowering developers to freely compose and turn creativity into unconstrained visual works.
We have made 12 upgrades across these three core dimensions. These are not just simple feature additions, but a solid foundation for building the next generation of data-driven applications. They all point to one goal:
to make ECharts powerful, reliable, and stable in the background, leaving the stage and spotlight for your creative expression.
Below, we introduce these twelve upgrades in detail:
More professional visual presentation
1. Brand New Default Theme
: Modern design language for professional data expression
2. Dynamic Theme Switching
: Seamless runtime theme switching for multi-theme scenarios
3. Dark Mode Support
: Automatically adapts to system dark/light mode for better UX
Expanding the boundaries of data expression
4. New Chord Chart
: Visualize complex relationships and distributions
5. New Beeswarm Chart
: Smartly expand overlapping data points into a honeycomb layout
6. New Scatter Jittering
: Add jitter to scatter plots for better readability of dense data
7. New Broken Axis
: Easily present data with large magnitude differences
8. Enhanced Stock Trading Charts
: Improved label capabilities and more out-of-the-box trading charts
Unleashing freedom of composition
9. New Matrix Coordinate System
: Freely combine chart types and components like a table
10. Enhanced Custom Series
: Support npm publishing and dynamic registration for code reuse
11. New Custom Charts
: Violin, contour, stage, bar range, and line range charts
12. Axis Label Optimization
: Smarter default axis label layout to prevent overflow and overlap
With these upgrades, Apache ECharts 6.0 helps users create more charts more flexibly and conveniently, truly achieving "unlimited possibilities in charting"!
Feature Details
1. Brand New Default Theme
During the development of ECharts 6.0, we analyzed real user scenarios and found that over 70% of developers use the default theme. This made us realize: an excellent default theme should not only be aesthetically pleasing but also meet the general needs of various business scenarios.
The new theme system uses design tokens to reconstruct colors, spacing, and other design elements,
making different chart types and components more harmonious and consistent
.
Although the 6.0 theme has significant changes from 5.x, we provide a
v5.js
theme file for developers who want to use new features but keep the old style for quick migration.
2. Dynamic Theme Switching
In previous versions, changing a chart's theme required disposing of the chart instance and re-initializing, which could negatively impact user experience due to repeated animations. In the new version, we implemented
dynamic theme switching
(see documentation), significantly improving the user experience.
3. Dark Mode Support
With dynamic theme registration and switching, a typical scenario is
listening to the system's dark mode and dynamically adjusting the chart's theme
.

data.title: No Comment (2010)
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了21世纪编程的核心在于实现想法，而非单纯追求技术。作者解释不开放评论的原因是为了避免负面技术讨论带来的影响，并分享了自己在编程初期的经验：面对看似不合理的代码时，发现深入了解背景和问题复杂性很重要。作者批评了工程师常有的草率批评态度，并以Flickr为例，强调积极的在线社区体验，认为应专注于分享实际经验而非无谓争辩。文章最后指出，编程讨论不应沉迷于技术争论，而应关注更有意义的交流。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：线上评论文化的优缺点及评论功能的价值

不同观点：
• **评论文化倾向于攻击性**：[getnormality] 指出，线上评论往往聚焦于挑错，试图证明原帖（OP）错误、无知或不合逻辑，而不是提供有见地的反馈。这种现象普遍存在，且人们往往没有意识到自己也在这样做。

• **私人交流 vs. 公开评论**：[dcminter] 通过引用侦探小说《Gaudy Night》中的一段对话，说明评论区往往引发强烈的情感反应，而私人信件交流则更为合适。评论区的公开性质容易导致过度批评，而非建设性反馈。

• **评论区的实用性与管理困难**：[stillpointlab] 和 [Brajeshwar] 提到，他们因为垃圾邮件和不良互动体验关闭了博客的评论功能。[stillpointlab] 还指出，现代网络评论往往受外部动机驱动，导致更多毒性。相比之下，[amitp] 认为评论区提供了很多有价值的信息和反馈，且通过外包管理（如 Disqus）可以有效减少管理负担。

• **评论区的价值与特定场景下的必要性**：[bombcar] 提到低流量博客的评论区可能包含对特定问题的唯一解决方案。[amitp] 强调评论区对他个人的学习与知识补充有很大帮助，并将其比作会议后的提问环节，具有潜在价值。

• **评论功能的设计与管理责任**：[Arch-TK] 指出，设计决策需要有详细文档支持，以避免依赖口头交流。这暗示了评论或文档的必要性。[taeric] 则认为，拥有评论区意味着要承担管理责任，防止滥用，而这可能增加负担。

补充讨论：
• **社交媒体与邮件反馈**：[thibaultamartin] 选择不在博客中嵌入评论，而是通过社交媒体和邮件获取反馈，认为这样能获得更有质量的互动。

• **评论区的争议性与网络对立现象**：[dsotm17] 提到，评论区常有“反对一切”的对立者，无论原帖内容如何，都会被挑错和反对，这种“反对主义”加剧了网络对立。

• **博客文化的变迁与短文趋势**：[LAC-Tech] 怀念过去的博客文化，认为短小精悍的文章更符合读者需求，并影响了他自己的写作风格。

争议焦点：评论区的价值与管理难题。一方认为评论区提供了有价值的互动和反馈，另一方则认为评论区容易引发无建设性的批评和不良互动，管理负担重且效果不佳。

44798434.article_content:
programming in the
twenty-first century
It's not about technology for its own sake. It's about being able to implement your ideas.
No Comment
I received a few emails after
last time
along the lines of "Oh. Perl. Homebrew CMS.
That's
why you don't allow people to post comments." Well, no, but it was definitely a conscious decision. The Web 2.0 answer is that I'm outsourcing comments to
reddit
and
Hacker News
. The real reason is this:
The negativity of online technical discussions makes me bitter, and even though I'm sometimes drawn to them I need to stay away.
To be fair, this isn't true only of technical discussions. Back when I was on
Usenet
, I took refuge from geeky bickering in a group about cooking...only to find people arguing the merits of
Miracle Whip
versus mayonnaise. Put enough people together and there are sure to be complaints and conflicting personal agendas. But with smart, technically-oriented people, I'd expect there to be more sharing of real experiences, but that's often not the case.
Here's a lesson I learned very early on after I started working full-time as a programmer (and that's a peculiar sentence for me to read, as I no longer program for a living). I'd be looking at some code at my desk, and it made no sense. Why would anyone write it like this? There's an obvious and cleaner way to approach the same problem.
So I'd go down the hall to the person who wrote it in the first place and start asking questions...and find out that I didn't have the whole picture, the problem was messier than it first appeared, and there were perfectly valid reasons for the code being that way. This happened again and again. Sometimes I did find a real flaw, but even then it may have only occurred with data that wasn't actually possible (because, for example, it was filtered by another part of the system). Talking face to face changed everything, because they could draw diagrams, pull out specs, and give concrete examples.
I think that initial knee-jerk "I've been looking at this for ten seconds and now let me explain the critical flaws" reaction is a common one among people with engineering mindsets. And that's not a good thing. I've seen this repeatedly, from people putting down programming languages for silly, superficial reasons (Perl's sigils, Python's enforced indentation), to ridiculous off-the-cuff put downs of new products (such as the predictions of doom in the
Slashdot announcement
of the original iPod in 2001).
The online community that I've had the most overwhelmingly positive experience with is the photo-sharing site
Flickr
. I'll keep talking about Flickr, because it played a big part in getting me out of some ruts, and I've seen more great photographs over the last five years than I would have seen in ten lifetimes otherwise. I know that if you dig around you can find tedious rants from equipment collectors, but I do a good job of avoiding those. I don't think I've ever seen real negativity in photo comments other than suggestions for different crops or the occasional technical criticisms. There are so many good photos to see that there's no reason to waste time with ones the don't appeal to me. That's supported by only allowing up-voting of photos (by adding a shot to your favorites); there's no way to formally register dislike.
Flickr gets my time, but most of the programming discussion sites don't.

• **评论区的实用性与管理困难**：[stillpointlab] 和 [Brajeshwar] 提到，他们因为垃圾邮件和不良互动体验关闭了博客的评论功能。[stillpointlab] 还指出，现代网络评论往往受外部动机驱动，导致更多毒性。相比之下，[amitp] 认为评论区提供了很多有价值的信息和反馈，且通过外包管理（如 Disqus）可以有效减少管理负担。

• **评论区的价值与特定场景下的必要性**：[bombcar] 提到低流量博客的评论区可能包含对特定问题的唯一解决方案。[amitp] 强调评论区对他个人的学习与知识补充有很大帮助，并将其比作会议后的提问环节，具有潜在价值。

• **评论功能的设计与管理责任**：[Arch-TK] 指出，设计决策需要有详细文档支持，以避免依赖口头交流。这暗示了评论或文档的必要性。[taeric] 则认为，拥有评论区意味着要承担管理责任，防止滥用，而这可能增加负担。

补充讨论：
• **社交媒体与邮件反馈**：[thibaultamartin] 选择不在博客中嵌入评论，而是通过社交媒体和邮件获取反馈，认为这样能获得更有质量的互动。

• **评论区的争议性与网络对立现象**：[dsotm17] 提到，评论区常有“反对一切”的对立者，无论原帖内容如何，都会被挑错和反对，这种“反对主义”加剧了网络对立。

• **博客文化的变迁与短文趋势**：[LAC-Tech] 怀念过去的博客文化，认为短小精悍的文章更符合读者需求，并影响了他自己的写作风格。

争议焦点：评论区的价值与管理难题。一方认为评论区提供了有价值的互动和反馈，另一方则认为评论区容易引发无建设性的批评和不良互动，管理负担重且效果不佳。

data.author: LAsteNERD

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Scorpius项目及其动态成像能力的讨论，包括其技术细节、应用场景以及未来前景。

不同观点：
• [bombela] 对文章中提到的7个月（7mths）表示困惑，认为应是微秒（μs）或纳秒（ns）级别的时间分辨率，并指出YouTube上已有纳秒甚至皮秒级别的成像演示，质疑100纳秒的时间分辨率有何特别之处。
• [LAsteNERD] 详细介绍了洛斯阿拉莫斯国家实验室的动态成像能力，强调了Scorpius项目在捕捉高分辨率、高速度图像方面的先进性，特别是其在核爆炸模拟中的应用。
• [meager_wikis] 对国家实验室的研究项目的可持续性表示担忧，认为由于预算削减和裁员，这些研究成果可能会逐渐减少。
• [tandr] 和 [dez11de] 以幽默方式表达了对缺乏实际图片证据的怀疑，提出了“不见图片，何以置信”的观点。
• [noobermin] 和 [throwaway290] 对项目未来可能被取消或资金不足表示担忧。
• [getpost] 将Scorpius项目与MIT展示的1万亿帧每秒的技术进行对比，指出二者应用场景不同，但强调了后者在时间分辨率上的先进性。
• [cco] 批评科学传播者未能提供读者期望看到的爆炸图像，认为这影响了传播效果。
• [zenmac] 和 [avodonosov] 直接询问是否能看到这些图像。
• [nxobject] 推测该项目与“无实际核武器的核弹头研究”相关。
• [paradox460] 提供了关于DARHT项目的更多信息，指出其与Scorpius项目有类似之处。
• [amelius] 关注图像是否与模拟结果相符，提出了对数据准确性的质疑。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Scorpius项目的时间分辨率是否特别以及其实际应用效果如何。
• 对科学传播中缺乏视觉证据的批评。
• 对国家实验室研究项目可持续性的担忧。
• 对图像数据真实性和可获取性的关注。

data.title: Proxmox Virtual Environment 9.0 with Debian 13 released
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: Proxmox Server Solutions发布了Proxmox Virtual Environment (VE) 9.0，该版本基于Debian 13 "Trixie"，采用Linux内核6.14.8-2，提升了硬件兼容性和性能。主要更新包括对厚配置LVM共享存储的快照支持，适用于iSCSI和FC SAN环境，并引入了SDN堆栈的"Fabrics"功能，支持复杂网络架构和自动故障转移。此外，高可用性（HA）集群增加了资源亲和性规则，优化资源分配，减少延迟。移动界面也经过重构，使用Rust框架Yew，提供更便捷的管理功能。该版本还更新了QEMU、LXC、Ceph和ZFS等开源技术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Proxmox作为虚拟化平台在不同使用场景中的优缺点，以及与其他平台（如VMware、XCP-ng、LXD）的对比。

不同观点：
• **支持Proxmox的观点**：
  - [BLKNSLVR] 从ESXi转向了Proxmox，因为Proxmox在消费级硬件上的兼容性更好，尤其是网络设备的兼容性。他还提到Proxmox的备份过程非常可靠，VM恢复也很稳定。
  - [riedel] 他们在一个四台机器的集群中使用Proxmox，认为其功能对业余管理员和用户来说恰到好处。他们也赞赏Proxmox的论坛资源，但对扩展性和自定义集成的复杂性提出了一些批评。
  - [nativeit] 长期使用Proxmox，并对其最新版本表示赞赏。

• **对Proxmox的功能和可用性提出改进意见**：
  - [redundantly] 认为Proxmox缺乏像VMware的VMFS那样的共享存储功能，无法在多个节点之间实现VM的故障转移。
  - [avtar] 认为Proxmox在集群环境中表现良好，但在单节点上的VM和容器配置管理不如LXD/Incus方便，尤其是版本控制方面。
  - [BodyCulture] 指出Proxmox缺乏官方支持的磁盘加密功能，用户需要自行解决，可能导致一些问题。
  - [krisknez] 希望Proxmox能有一个用于端口转发的UI，而不必通过终端操作。

• **对Proxmox升级和兼容性的关注**：
  - [PeterStuer] 从Hyper-V转向Proxmox，关心Proxmox的升级过程是否顺利。
  - [grmone] 对Proxmox使用的Linux内核版本提出疑问，担心其是否自行 backport 安全补丁。
  - [throw0101c] 提供Proxmox VE 9.0的发布亮点链接，并提到XCP-ng作为一个替代选项，邀请使用过两者的人比较其优缺点。

• **关于Proxmox安装和UI技术的讨论**：
  - [Takennickname] 询问Proxmox是否一直可以安装在Debian上，回忆过去版本（如7.x）可能不支持此功能。
  - [xattt] 表示由于需要为集成Intel显卡实现SR-IOV功能，暂时不考虑转到Proxmox。
  - [yla92] 首次听说Yew框架（由Rust编写并编译为WASM的前端框架），并询问其他人是否有使用经验。

补充讨论：
- Proxmox的备份和恢复功能被广泛认可，尤其是在小型和业余环境中表现出色。
- 用户对Proxmox在扩展性和自定义集成方面的复杂性表示关注，尤其是与API和UI相关的自定义。
- 对Proxmox的磁盘加密和共享存储功能的需求被提及，显示出部分用户对安全性和高级功能的需求。
- 用户在考虑Proxmox时，对其升级过程的平滑程度和硬件兼容性表示关注。
- 提到了XCP-ng作为Proxmox的替代选项，引发了一些关于两者优缺点的讨论。

44798035.article_content:
Proxmox Virtual Environment 9.0 with Debian 13 released
August 05, 2025
Download:
English
German
VIENNA, Austria – August 05, 2025 –
Leading open-source server solutions provider Proxmox Server Solutions GmbH (henceforth "Proxmox"), celebrating its 20th year of innovation, today announced the release of Proxmox Virtual Environment (VE) 9.0. Main highlight of this update is a modernized core built upon Debian 13 “Trixie”, ensuring a robust foundation for the platform.
Proxmox VE 9.0 further introduces significant advancements in both storage and networking capabilities, addressing critical enterprise demands. A highlight is the long-awaited support for snapshots on thick-provisioned LVM shared storage, improving storage management capabilities especially for enterprise users with Fibre Channel (FC) or iSCSI SAN environments. With newly added “fabric” support for Software-Defined Networking (SDN), administrators can construct highly complex and scalable network architectures.
Highlights in Proxmox Virtual Environment 9.0
Debian 13 “Trixie” at the core
This core update is based on Debian 13 “Trixie”, bringing the latest Debian release as foundation for Proxmox VE including newer packages, improved hardware support, and enhanced security. Proxmox VE is using a newer Linux kernel 6.14.8-2 as stable default enhancing hardware compatibility and performance.
Also, updates to the latest versions of leading open-source technologies for virtual environments like QEMU 10.0.2, LXC 6.0.4, Ceph Squid 19.2.3, and ZFS 2.3.3 are included. ZFS now supports adding new devices to existing RAIDZ pools with minimal downtime. For existing users of Proxmox VE 8.4 or older versions, an extensively tested and detailed upgrade path is available to enable a smooth upgrade.
Snapshots for thick-provisioned LVM shared storage
Virtual Machines (VMs) utilizing thick-provisioned LVM shared storages, such as those backed by iSCSI or FC-based SANs, now benefit from snapshot functionality out of the box. This is achieved by implementing snapshots as volume chains, where a volume based on a snapshot only records differences to its parent snapshot volume. Directory, NFS, and CIFS storages also gain additional support for snapshots as volume chains.
This new feature provides a powerful and highly requested capability for customers with traditional SAN infrastructure who have historically relied on clustered file systems. While direct integrations from many storage vendors continue to grow, this new feature closes the gap by providing a storage-independent solution for snapshots. This gives customers the independence to seamlessly manage their snapshots regardless of their hardware, without compromising on convenience.
New Fabrics feature for the SDN stack
This release enhances the SDN capabilities with the introduction of an SDN Fabrics feature, designed to simplify the configuration and management of complex routed networks. Engineered for reliability, SDN Fabrics facilitates multiple paths between nodes and automatic failover across Network Interface Cards (NICs), enabling the configuration of robust two-layer spine-leaf architectures for improved network redundancy and performance.
This new feature simplifies the management of dynamically routed networks which can for example be used as Ethernet VPN (EVPN) underlay or full-mesh networks for Ceph. The SDN stack in Proxmox VE gains support for two different routing protocols, OpenFabric and OSPF, and provides intuitive tools for the simplified configuration and precise management of those dynamic routing protocols.
Affinity rules in High Availability (HA) clusters
The Proxmox team introduces HA resource affinity rules to enable fine-grained control and flexibility over resource placement in HA clusters, ensuring optimal performance, enhanced resiliency, and minimized latency for critical workloads. To better control complex, interconnected applications, the new HA Resource Affinity Rules allow administrators to precisely define how virtual machines and other HA resources are distributed across a cluster.
Interdependent HA resources, such as for example an application server and its associated database, can be kept together on the same physical node to minimize network latency. For services requiring maximum redundancy, like multiple VMs running the same mission-critical application, the rules can ensure these instances are kept on different nodes. This increases fault tolerance and ensures resiliency even during HA failovers.
Enhanced mobile interface
The Proxmox VE mobile interface has been thoroughly reworked, using the new Proxmox widget toolkit powered by the Rust-based Yew framework. The redesigned interface provides quick access to service overviews and includes essential management functions, including starting and stopping virtual guests and basic configuration. It is now easier than ever for users to access fundamental functionalities of Proxmox VE directly from their mobile browsers.

  - [BLKNSLVR] 从ESXi转向了Proxmox，因为Proxmox在消费级硬件上的兼容性更好，尤其是网络设备的兼容性。他还提到Proxmox的备份过程非常可靠，VM恢复也很稳定。
  - [riedel] 他们在一个四台机器的集群中使用Proxmox，认为其功能对业余管理员和用户来说恰到好处。他们也赞赏Proxmox的论坛资源，但对扩展性和自定义集成的复杂性提出了一些批评。
  - [nativeit] 长期使用Proxmox，并对其最新版本表示赞赏。

• **对Proxmox的功能和可用性提出改进意见**：
  - [redundantly] 认为Proxmox缺乏像VMware的VMFS那样的共享存储功能，无法在多个节点之间实现VM的故障转移。
  - [avtar] 认为Proxmox在集群环境中表现良好，但在单节点上的VM和容器配置管理不如LXD/Incus方便，尤其是版本控制方面。
  - [BodyCulture] 指出Proxmox缺乏官方支持的磁盘加密功能，用户需要自行解决，可能导致一些问题。
  - [krisknez] 希望Proxmox能有一个用于端口转发的UI，而不必通过终端操作。

• **对Proxmox升级和兼容性的关注**：
  - [PeterStuer] 从Hyper-V转向Proxmox，关心Proxmox的升级过程是否顺利。
  - [grmone] 对Proxmox使用的Linux内核版本提出疑问，担心其是否自行 backport 安全补丁。
  - [throw0101c] 提供Proxmox VE 9.0的发布亮点链接，并提到XCP-ng作为一个替代选项，邀请使用过两者的人比较其优缺点。

• **关于Proxmox安装和UI技术的讨论**：
  - [Takennickname] 询问Proxmox是否一直可以安装在Debian上，回忆过去版本（如7.x）可能不支持此功能。
  - [xattt] 表示由于需要为集成Intel显卡实现SR-IOV功能，暂时不考虑转到Proxmox。
  - [yla92] 首次听说Yew框架（由Rust编写并编译为WASM的前端框架），并询问其他人是否有使用经验。

补充讨论：
- Proxmox的备份和恢复功能被广泛认可，尤其是在小型和业余环境中表现出色。
- 用户对Proxmox在扩展性和自定义集成方面的复杂性表示关注，尤其是与API和UI相关的自定义。
- 对Proxmox的磁盘加密和共享存储功能的需求被提及，显示出部分用户对安全性和高级功能的需求。
- 用户在考虑Proxmox时，对其升级过程的平滑程度和硬件兼容性表示关注。

data.title: Consider using Zstandard and/or LZ4 instead of Deflate
data.author: marklit
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在PNG图像格式中使用Zstandard和LZ4压缩算法替代Deflate的建议，以提升读取和写入速度。这些新的无损压缩算法由开源社区维护，没有专利问题，且在其他领域（如Khronos KTX2 GPU纹理格式）已有应用。Zstandard和LZ4能显著加快处理速度，特别适合需要频繁读写PNG文件的工作流。虽然还有其他更简单的快速压缩格式（如QOI），但它们可能需要改变图像压缩前的处理方式。本文提议将Zstandard作为未来PNG版本的选项之一，并标记为需要讨论的改进建议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PNG标准及其替代方案的优缺点，包括压缩效率、解压缩速度和广泛的支持性。

不同观点：
• **支持JPEG XL**：e-topy认为JPEG XL具有渐进解码、小文件体积、支持HDR和动画等优点，且解码速度更快，因此优于新的PNG标准。
• **质疑ZPNG的优势**：arp242通过数据比较指出，ZPNG在压缩效果上没有显著优势，仅在解压时间上略有提升，整体不值得采用。
• **PNG压缩优化**：pornel提到通过针对PNG数据优化的deflate算法可以显著提升压缩速度，且保持标准兼容性。
• **自定义压缩算法**：physicles分享了自己在处理大型非图像数据时的经验，通过使用Snappy和Simple8b等自定义算法，获得了20倍的解压速度提升。
• **ZStandard的外部字典**：jasonthorsness提出ZStandard的外部字典功能可能对PNG压缩有效，但需要实验验证。
• **ZSTD的局限性**：citrin_ru指出尽管ZSTD性能优越，但其在多种语言和平台上的支持不如PNG广泛，且对硬件要求更高。
• **替代方案的实际应用**：zX41ZdbW分享了自己项目中使用zstd编码替代PNG生成的经验，取得了良好效果。
• **后向兼容的重要性**：bawolff认为保持PNG的兼容性很重要，新的格式应避免与旧格式不兼容。
• **LZ4的速度优势**：electroly认为LZ4在速度上具有优势，特别是在服务器和客户端都可控的情况下。
• **QOI的潜力**：willvarfar建议考虑使用QOI，因其在压缩效率上优于PNG，且进一步压缩后效果更佳。

补充讨论：
• **PNG的历史和现状**：encom和HocusLocus提到PNG的历史问题，如未支持动画导致GIF依然流行，并认为PNG无需大改动。
• **Deflate的现状**：privatelypublic质疑Deflate在当前的任何优势，仅在极低硬件配置下可能仍有价值。
• **内容协商的状态**：hughw提出内容协商在浏览器中的应用情况不明，值得进一步探讨。

争议焦点：
• **ZPNG是否值得采用**：一方认为ZPNG在压缩效果和解压速度上的优势不明显，另一方则认为其优化仍有价值。
• **PNG的改进方向**：一方认为PNG无需大改动，保持兼容性更重要，另一方则认为应尝试新的格式如JPEG XL或QOI。

One of the issues we have with .PNG is slow read/write times. There are now new lossless open source codecs without patent concerns, such as Zstandard (maintained by Facebook) or LZ4:
https://facebook.github.io/zstd/
https://github.com/lz4/lz4
Zstandard is used by the new Khronos KTX2 GPU texture format specification. I propose that it be added as an option to a future version of .PNG. The possible speedups are quite significant, and for users that read and write a lot of .PNG's as part of their data processing pipelines the speedups will be high value improvements.
There are also other far simpler but even faster codecs being developed, such as .QOI's, but using this would likely require changing or not filtering the image before compression:
https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=29328750

data.title: Show HN: Whittle – A shrinking word game
data.author: babel16
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对某款字谜游戏的反馈与建议

不同观点：
• [jsnell] 认为游戏中的双重目标（消除所有字母和找到所有单词）令人困惑，尤其是因为游戏通过颜色提示推动玩家完成后者，这被认为较为乏味。此外，桌面版的UI缺乏悬停效果，点击字母时没有反馈，建议至少改变光标样式。
• [duncancarroll] 提到游戏结束时缺乏“胜利”提示，让人感到困惑，期望有某种结束提示或新一轮的指引。
• [jangerhofer] 指出空格也是可消除的字符，对初学者来说可能不明显。
• [pimlottc] 反馈初始状态不明确，字母点击不够直观，尤其是与其他类似游戏相比，底部的未标记标签和点击区域让人困惑，建议增加标签和交互效果。
• [c22] 将游戏与自己曾经玩的类似游戏做比较，描述了不同的玩法规则，认为这款游戏是另一种形式的文字游戏。
• [davidsojevic] 和 [hackyhacky] 提到游戏在多个浏览器中出现崩溃问题，无法开始游戏，错误提示为 `G is null` 或 `puzzleLog` 无法读取。
• [yobananaboy] 建议如果目标是将字母减少到一个就应该触发胜利状态，而不是让玩家手动重置。
• [jessecoleman] 提到自己开发的文字游戏与该游戏有相似之处，但实际玩法不同，并称赞了该游戏的UX设计。
• [teach] 质疑是否每局游戏都能将字母减少到一个，并以8月4日的谜题为例说明其难度。
• [kps] 建议游戏应尊重系统的 `:prefers-color-scheme` 设置，可能是对夜间模式或主题颜色的需求。
• [spadros] 认为游戏需要一个提示功能，自己完成了所有单词但未能将字母减少到零，寻求帮助。
• [fao_] 表示非常喜欢游戏，但分享按钮在PC版的Firefox上无法使用。
• [werds] 开玩笑地祝贺游戏即将被《纽约时报》收购，类似于Wordle的成功。

补充讨论：
• 游戏的UI和UX设计是主要讨论点之一，尤其是点击反馈和视觉提示的不足。
• 双重目标的设定和游戏结束的提示不清是另一个焦点，部分玩家认为找到所有单词的任务乏味且不明确。
• 一些技术问题如浏览器崩溃和功能按钮失效也被多个用户提到。
• 部分玩家对游戏的策略性和难度提出了疑问和建议，如是否总能将字母减少到一个以及增加提示功能的需求。

data.title: Ozempic shows anti-aging effects in trial
data.author: amichail
data.article_summary: 一项随机对照试验对108名患有HIV相关脂肪代谢障碍的患者进行了研究，发现每周使用Ozempic（司美鲁肽）治疗32周后，受试者的生物学年龄平均逆转了3.1年。研究使用表观遗传时钟测量生物学衰老，发现最显著的抗衰老效果体现在炎症系统和大脑，衰老被延迟了近5年。研究人员认为，司美鲁肽通过改善脂肪分布和减少炎症，从而减缓细胞衰老。尽管结果令人鼓舞，但研究者 caution 不要过早将Ozempic广泛用于抗衰老治疗，但指出该药物在抗衰老领域的潜力巨大。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕semaglutides（如Ozempic）的争议及其潜在的抗衰老和减肥效果

不同观点：
• 一些人（如some_random）认为公众对semaglutides的仇恨是不合理的，超越了谨慎或怀疑，变成了一种非理性的恐惧。
• Pitpatagain指出，该研究仅针对HIV相关脂肪代谢障碍的人群，其结果未必适用于普通人群。
• Lurking_swe认为研究结果显而易见，肥胖导致的炎症和脂肪分布问题加速衰老，而Ozempic通过减肥减轻了这些问题，类似于证明雨增加湿度。
• Charlie0和jsbg质疑，Ozempic的抗衰老效果是否仅仅源于体重减轻本身，而非药物的特定效果。
• Getpost引用Ben Bikman的播客，讨论GLP-1药物的历史和潜在风险，指出早期小剂量使用可能更安全。
• Neves警告不要轻信“奇迹药物”的宣传，分享其母亲因服用Ozempic出现严重副作用的个人经历，强调长期效果仍不明确。
• Lysecret对semaglutides的更多积极效果表示兴奋。
• Wolfi1质疑“生物年龄”是否有一个明确的定义。
• V__对使用表观遗传时钟的研究持怀疑态度，认为这些研究的结果误差较大，不可靠。
• Thurn关注semaglutides的价格问题，询问是否有可能在印度等国家获得价格更低的仿制药。
• Xeromal和Scrozart提醒大家关注研究本身，而不是依赖个人轶事和意见。
• Heraldgeezer提倡通过禁食而非药物来达到健康效果。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于semaglutides的实际效果和安全性，尤其是长期使用的未知风险。
• 有人质疑“生物年龄”和表观遗传时钟的科学可靠性。
• 个人经历（如neves的母亲）为讨论增加了对药物副作用的实际担忧。
• 价格和获取途径也是讨论的重要部分，特别是在低成本仿制药的可行性上。

44798410.article_content:
Key Insights
A randomized controlled trial of 108 people with HIV-associated lipohypertrophy found that weekly Ozempic treatment for 32 weeks reversed biological age by an average of 3.1 years.
The study used epigenetic clocks to measure biological aging, showing the most pronounced anti-aging effects in the inflammatory system and brain, where aging was delayed by almost 5 years.
Researchers believe the anti-aging effects stem from semaglutide's ability to improve fat distribution and reduce inflammation, both major drivers of cellular aging.
The diabetes drug Ozempic has demonstrated remarkable anti-aging effects in the first clinical trial to directly measure its impact on biological aging, with participants becoming an average of 3.1 years biologically younger after 32 weeks of treatment. The findings provide the strongest evidence yet that GLP-1 drugs like semaglutide may offer benefits far beyond their established roles in diabetes management and weight loss.
First Direct Clinical Evidence of Anti-Aging Effects
Varun Dwaraka from diagnostics company TruDiagnostic in Lexington, Kentucky, led a randomized controlled trial involving 108 people with HIV-associated lipohypertrophy, a condition characterized by excess fat accumulation and accelerated cellular aging. Half the participants received weekly Ozempic injections for 32 weeks, while the other half received a placebo.
The researchers used epigenetic clocks to assess biological aging - sophisticated tools that identify patterns of DNA methylation, chemical tags that affect gene activity and shift predictably with age. These patterns can be accelerated or slowed by lifestyle factors, meaning biological age can differ significantly from chronological age.
"Those on semaglutide became, on average, 3.1 years biologically younger by the end of the study," Dwaraka reported. The placebo group showed no significant change in biological age over the same period.
Organ-Specific Anti-Aging Benefits
The anti-aging effects weren't uniform across all body systems. The research team found that semaglutide slowed biological aging in several organs and systems, with the most dramatic improvements occurring in the inflammatory system and brain, where the drug appeared to delay biological aging by almost 5 years. Significant benefits were also observed in the heart and kidneys.
"Semaglutide may not only slow the rate of ageing, but in some individuals partially reverse it," Dwaraka noted, highlighting the potential for the drug to actually turn back the biological clock rather than simply slowing its progression.
Mechanisms Behind the Anti-Aging Effects
The researchers believe semaglutide's anti-aging properties stem from its effects on fat distribution and metabolic health. Excess fat around organs triggers the release of pro-aging molecules that alter DNA methylation in key aging-related genes. By reducing this harmful fat accumulation and preventing low-grade inflammation - both major drivers of epigenetic aging - semaglutide appears to create a more youthful biological environment.
Randy Seeley from the University of Michigan Medical School expressed little surprise at the findings, explaining that the drugs "reduce the metabolic burden on a wide range of cells and lower inflammation. Both are major drivers of ageing in many different types of cells." However, he believes much of the benefit stems not from semaglutide's direct cellular effects, but from broader improvements to overall health.
Broader Implications and Future Directions
While the study focused specifically on people with HIV-associated lipohypertrophy, the biological pathways affected by semaglutide aren't unique to this condition. "Therefore, it is plausible that similar effects on epigenetic ageing could be observed in other populations," Dwaraka explained, suggesting the anti-aging benefits could extend to the general population.
Despite the promising results, Dwaraka cautioned against rushing to prescribe semaglutide broadly as an anti-aging therapy. "Prescribing it more broadly as an anti-ageing therapy is premature," he stated. However, he noted that the study adds momentum to ongoing efforts to repurpose existing drugs for age-related problems, which could speed approval processes and reduce the risk of unexpected side effects.
The research represents a significant milestone in understanding the full therapeutic potential of GLP-1 drugs, which have already gained prominence for treating type 2 diabetes and obesity, and are being explored for cardiovascular disease, addiction, and dementia. "Semaglutide may well emerge as one of the most promising candidates in this space," Dwaraka concluded.

data.title: US Coast Guard Report on Titan Submersible
data.author: rwmj
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OceanGate的TITAN潜艇事故原因及其背后的决策和文化问题

不同观点：
• dwheeler：事故的主要原因是物理因素，包括使用未经认证的碳纤维复合材料用于深海潜水器。报告指出，碳纤维在深海高压环境下承受压应力时表现不佳，且没有获得任何国家或国际标准的认可。此外，人為决策，如公司安全文化的缺失和管理层的傲慢态度，也是导致事故的重要原因。
• TheCleric：此次事故是"快速行动、打破常规"和"反对监管"文化的逻辑结果。许多安全规则都是基于血的教训写成的，并非无意义的官僚主义。OceanGate忽视了这些规则，导致了悲剧的发生。
• post_break：尽管潜艇的设计和材料有诸多缺陷，如碳纤维和控制器的缺陷，但它在前几次航行中幸存了下来。Stockton Rush忽视了警告信号，最终导致了事故的发生。
• cogman10：调查显示潜艇的实时监控系统发出了警告，但OceanGate没有采取行动。他们不仅忽视了数据，也没有进行预防性维护或妥善储存潜艇，这是严重的管理失误。
• ItsBob：从Netflix纪录片中了解到，事故发生时乘客在毫秒级别内瞬间消失，这种极端的物理现象让人感到震惊和不可思议。
• ridgeguy：纤维增强复合材料在拉伸时表现出色，但在压缩时表现极差。选择这种材料用于潜艇设计从一开始就是个错误。
• ortusdux：美国海岸警卫队的听证会，尤其是Matthew McCoy的证词，揭示了公司内部的许多问题，提供了有价值的背景信息。
• bouchard：Stockton Rush希望像SpaceX在太空领域一样，成为海洋探索领域的颠覆者。然而，他的冒险精神最终导致了灾难。
• Luker88：作为消费者，是否需要自己对海洋探险公司进行背景调查？海洋工业似乎缺乏监管，或者公司无视规则，这都是令人担忧的问题。
• nathan_compton：事故既有悲剧性，也有讽刺意味。Rush的墓志铭可以写上"快速行动、打破常规"。
• danjl：OceanGate的商业模式基于认为现有法规和设计限制过于保守，最终导致了客户的死亡代价。
• nodesocket：碳纤维在多次测试中表现不佳，其他深水潜艇使用钛材是有原因的。Rush坚持使用碳纤维是不合理的。

补充讨论：
• kelseyfrog：提到"这将成为一个切斯特顿式的围栏"，暗示未来人们可能会从这次事故中吸取教训，建立新的安全规则和标准。

争议焦点：
• 碳纤维材料是否适合用于深海潜艇的争论。
• OceanGate管理层对安全警告的忽视以及对传统安全规则的蔑视。
• 消费者在参与高风险活动时应承担的责任以及行业监管的有效性。

data.title: Ask HN: Have you ever regretted open-sourcing something?
data.author: paulwilsonn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源项目的利弊与个人经历

不同观点：
• **开源项目的商业化潜力**：
  - [Aurornis] 提到见过开源项目创建者后悔没有将其商业化，认为如果项目闭源并商业化可能会带来财富。
  - [bob1029] 主张对复杂产品采取源代码可见但收费的模式，认为开源不一定适合所有类型的软件。

• **开源项目带来的负面体验**：
  - [pentamassiv] 描述了自己维护的开源项目被大公司使用，但申请该公司的职位却被拒绝，感到错失了受益于自己劳动成果的机会。
  - [erulabs] 分享了自己在年轻时因开源代码质量差而受到批评，导致长时间失去编码欲望。
  - [doawoo] 提到开源项目带来了经济资助，但也引发了其他开发者的嫉妒和无理要求。
  - [blibble] 后悔开源了自己的作品，因为它们被AI技术使用而没有得到应有的 attribution（署名）。
  - [acheong08] 后悔开源了一个个人项目，因为其他用户利用其功能绕过官方限制，最终导致项目失效。
  - [throwaway889900] 因未满足用户需求而收到死亡威胁，决定退出开源。

• **开源项目的法律与公司限制**：
  - [aurumque] 描述了自己努力争取公司开源一个工具，但因公司限制无法维护项目，最终对开源感到失望。
  - [greyface-] 试图通过公司审核委员会开源个人项目，但因程序繁琐和不确定的知识产权问题而放弃。

• **开源项目的维护负担**：
  - [ptmcc] 提到自己开源的项目收到过多的功能请求和不合理的bug报告，导致对分享个人项目感到不满。
  - [incomingpain] 指出开源项目带来的维护负担和用户需求使得开发者难以长期维护多个项目。

补充讨论：
• **开源项目与误解**：
  - [TheTon] 分享了自己项目被误认为是Google产品而引起广泛关注的经历，质疑这种误解是否是Google Code关闭的原因。
  
• **开源项目的侵权问题**：
  - [galad87] 提到自己以GPL2许可发布的代码被他人稍作修改后在Mac App Store上出售，显示了开源项目可能遭遇的侵权问题。

争议焦点：
• 开源项目的商业化与社区贡献之间的矛盾。
• 开源项目带来的负面体验与开发者期望之间的差距。
• 开源项目在法律、公司政策和个人利益之间的复杂关系。

data.title: Small changes that made our daily stand-ups more useful
data.author: dkoprowski
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了如何改善敏捷开发中的每日站会，使其更具价值而非流于形式或浪费时间。站会常被视为负担，因其容易变成冗长的状态报告，使参与者感到无聊且缺乏实际帮助。作者通过实践，提出了一些有效利用站会的建议：

1. **站会的真正目的**：应聚焦于同步当天的计划和优先事项，尽早发现障碍，鼓励团队协作和知识共享，增强团队责任感和支持。
   
2. **常见陷阱**：避免陷入“报告模式”和知识孤岛，报告模式导致枯燥、脱离和错失协作机会；知识孤岛则让重要信息无法共享。

3. **实际例子**：通过具体例子展示如何改进站会发言，使其更具针对性、上下文背景，并专注于当天的目标和需求，促进团队协作。

最终，站会应成为团队协作、支持和解决问题的起点，而非单纯的状态汇报。

不同观点：

  - [agentultra] 认为每日站会是微观管理的体现，只有在没有经理参与且团队自主时才有效。
  - [hshdhdhj4444] 指出站会的社交压力让人不愿承认自己没做什么，而且团队已经在聊天中提前沟通了问题。
  - [theboywho] 引用心理学观点，认为站会浪费时间，实际工作中的同步沟通已经足够。

44800943.article_content:
Share
Daily stand-ups are a cornerstone of agile software development – but often they’re seen as a burden or a distraction. Why? Because they frequently devolve into long status reports that bore participants and add little real value.
Others see it as a waste of time or such regular part of their day, that it doesn’t deserve a second though.
During the past two years, together with my team, I worked on improving our daily to transform it to a tool that helps every participant to kickstart their day. In this blogpost I share tips that might be useful also for your team.
What Is the Purpose of a Daily Meeting – and What It Isn’t
I often see complains on developers forums that a daily meetings are used only as a control mechanism – a way for managers to check up on what everyone did yesterday.
Since I trust my team, I’ve designed our daily meetings to bring real value to developers.
Instead of treating the daily as a status report, we use it as a chance for:
syncing plans
and priorities for the current day,
signaling blockers
early so the team can help,
encouraging
collaboration
and
knowledge sharing
,
building a sense of
team ownership
and support.
I don’t want a daily meeting where everyone focuses on yesterday. I want one where we help each other move forward.
While it’s tempting to ditch the “what I did yesterday” report entirely to avoid turning meetings into monotonous recaps,
don’t abandon it completely
.
Question about yesterday can reveal dysfunctions or blocker early, like when team members admit, “I didn’t get much done due to back-to-back meetings,” signaling a need for broader changes to free up focus time. My point is to
keep it brief and tie it to today’s plans
for maximum value.
The purpose of a daily meeting is to collaboratively kickstart the day by aligning individual plans with team goals, supporting each other, and uncovering blockers.
Common Pitfalls: Reporting Mode and Knowledge Silos
Many teams get stuck in the “reporting mode,” where each developer spends most of their time describing their own yesterday’s work, often justifying themselves.
This leads to:
Monotony:
Hearing detailed reports every day gets boring fast.
Disengagement:
People stop listening or multitask in background.
Missed collaboration:
Blockers and requests for help don’t get surfaced.
Knowledge silos:
Important insights stay locked inside individuals.
That is my biggest nemesis
. I always felt that purely reporting meetings are a burden, a waste of energy, those are spreading mistrust in the team. It might work in some setups – I don’t deny that there is a use case. Although, in a workflow that I value, I wanted to have a meeting, where we plan the upcoming day to spend the time productive.
Real-World Daily Stand-Up Examples
Avoid: The Classic “Justifying My Existence” Update
Read through this daily status update and think how could it be improved:
Yesterday, I fixed a bug assigned to me. Then, I attended all-hands meeting and I had to go out for some time. Then we had retro. I also started a new story from to-do. Today, I will continue working on it.
Key Issues:
Vague:
No specific details on what was fixed or which story was started.
No Context:
Generic terms like “assigned to me,” “new story,” and “continue working on it” do not provide actionable info. What story that dev is even mentioning? No one knows.
No Request for Help:
No mention of needing assistance or collaboration.
No Value for Team:
Update is mostly a personal log; teammates cannot offer help or gain insight.
Focused on Past:
Update is mostly a report on yesterday’s activities, not today’s goals or blockers.
After listening to such update, teammates wouldn’t think of how they could collaborate. They would be lost, forced to ask additional questions or simply fall back and wait for the next person.
Improved: A Specific, Team-Focused Daily Update
Here is my attempt to improve such update:
Yesterday, I fixed a sidebar flickering bug. Please review my PR soon as it is annoying for customers. I started a video player story that we discussed at the last refinement. Since it’s my first time working with the player module, I’d appreciate pairing up or any tips from someone familiar with it.
Today, my focus is on wiring up the play/pause functionality. Happy to sync after stand-up if anyone’s available.
What’s Improved:
Specific:
Names the details of bug and story.
Contextual:
Explains the urgency (“annoying for customers”) and the origin of the story (“discussed at last refinement”).
Focus on Today:
Highlights what is planned for today and where support is needed.
Expressed openness:
Invites help both for pairing and advice–not just passive review.
Offered a sync:
Proactively asks for a follow-up, lowering the barrier for collaboration.
Additionally, when a Jira board (or whatever you use) is on a shared display the team should have no problem with following what this dev is talking about and how to help them.
How We Structure Our Daily Meetings to Create Val

本文讨论了如何改善敏捷开发中的每日站会，使其更具价值而非流于形式或浪费时间。站会常被视为负担，因其容易变成冗长的状态报告，使参与者感到无聊且缺乏实际帮助。作者通过实践，提出了一些有效利用站会的建议：

3. **实际例子**：通过具体例子展示如何改进站会发言，使其更具针对性、上下文背景，并专注于当天的目标和需求，促进团队协作。

最终，站会应成为团队协作、支持和解决问题的起点，而非单纯的状态汇报。

data.title: Google agrees to pause AI workloads when power demand spikes
data.author: twapi
data.article_summary: Google宣布，将在电力需求高峰时暂停非必要的AI工作负载，以保护电网。这一举措是在与印第安纳密歇根电力公司和田纳西流域管理局达成协议后做出的。在炎热夏季，居民大量使用空调导致电网压力增加时，若能源需求激增或电网出现问题，Google将通过调整数据中心耗电量或延迟非紧急任务来减少电力使用，这一过程称为“需求响应”。尽管AI模型训练耗电巨大，但一些工作负载无需全天候运行，可以在电网压力较小时进行。Google还在投资可再生能源和核能，以应对数据中心耗电问题。不过，Google无法随意暂停云客户的AI任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电力需求响应、人工智能（AI）公司的能源消耗及其对社会和环境的影响

不同观点：
• [acc_297] 认为，当前我们过快地增加了电力消耗，尤其是在实现碳强度减少目标之前，推动了大规模的电力需求。担忧市场力量无法有效监管跨国科技公司，这些公司可以几乎不受限制地选择数据中心的地点，并将计算基础设施的外部性转移到远离付费客户的地方。

• [kerblang] 强调“需求响应”是电力公司和大型客户之间长期存在的做法，不仅仅是针对工业用户，普通消费者也可以通过使用电力公司提供的自动调节温控器，在高峰负荷期间减少用电，并获得折扣。

• [HocusLocus] 指出，AI公司正试图通过公开讨论其对电网电力需求的影响，来展示自己作为“良好的企业管理者”。然而，北美地区依赖天然气和石油能源，拒绝核能，这将导致问题。AI公司不仅没有创造直接的就业机会，反而因其能源消耗引发更多的反对，最终可能被迫迁离城市，甚至最终可能被驱赶到“轨道上”。

• [Pet_Ant] 提出，如果AI训练仅在电力过剩时进行，并取代类似比特币挖矿的能源浪费行为，可能对社会产生积极影响。

• [codemac] 认为，数据中心（DC）运营商普遍与当地电网有需求响应协议，并且在风暴或需求增加期间与上游电力供应商密切合作，极少会危害整个社区的电网安全。对数据中心运营的担忧往往是过度紧张的表现。

• [im3w1l] 关注AI训练中的电力成本，认为电力成本可能已经超过芯片折旧成本，成为主要的训练开支。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是AI公司是否在通过展示对能源问题的关注来提升其企业形象，而实际上这些公司对当地能源基础设施和环境带来了负面影响（HocusLocus的观点）。
• 另一个讨论点是，电力需求响应机制在工业用户和普通消费者之间的应用是否公平，以及如何在全球范围内有效监管跨国科技公司的能源消耗（acc_297和kerblang的观点）。
• 对AI训练能源消耗的未来影响和解决方案的探讨，包括将其与比特币挖矿进行类比，提出利用过剩电力进行训练的潜在益处（Pet_Ant的观点）。
• 对电力成本在AI训练中的重要性及其对行业的影响进行了简要分析（im3w1l的观点）。

Off-Prem

Google agrees to pause AI workloads to protect the grid when power demand spikes
19
On hot summer days, air conditioning is rather more important than search summaries
Tobias Mann
Mon 4 Aug 2025
//
22:58 UTC
Google will pause non-essential AI workloads to protect power grids, the advertising giant announced on Monday.
The web giant already does this sort of thing for non-essential workloads like processing YouTube vids, which it moves to datacenters where power is available rather than continuing to run them in places demand for energy strains the grid.
Under an agreement with Indiana Michigan Power (I&M) and the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA), Google will use the same techniques for AI workloads.
The announcement comes as states served by the power companies brace for a heat wave that will likely strain the grid as residents use air conditioners and increase demand for energy. Amid debate about datacenters’ consumption of power and water, the last thing that the Chocolate Factory needs is folks blaming its AI Mode search function for a power outage when temperatures top 100°F (37.7°C).
Under the agreement, if energy demand surges or there's a disruption in the grid due to extreme weather, I&M and TVA can now request that Google reduce its power use by rescheduling workloads or limiting non-urgent tasks until the issue is resolved.
By dynamically adjusting how much power its bit barns are allowed to consume, a process Google calls “demand response”, the web giant argues that new datacenters can be interconnected more quickly — presumably because utilities are less concerned about them causing brown outs or outages.
"By including load flexibility in our overall energy plan, we can manage AI-driven growth even where power generation and transmission are constrained," Google wrote in a
blog post
on Monday.
Training and running AI models can easily consume tens or even hundreds of megawatts of power for hours, days, or weeks at a time, depending on how big or complex they are. However certain workloads don't need to run 24/7. Advancements in checkpointing mean that a model could be trained exclusively at night when grid capacity is at its greatest.
Datacenter demand-response is still a nascent technology and is only being employed at a handful of Google bit barns. Further complicating the matter, the approach is also incompatible with certain high-demand workloads, such as Search, Maps, or its cloud business, Google notes.
AI going critical: Hyundai to help build nuclear-powered datacenter in Texas
Tony Blair Institute: UK needs bit barns to lead in AI deployment, not training
Altman embraces inner Viking, raids Europe with 100K GPU supercluster in Norway
Datacenter lobby blows a fuse over EU efficiency proposals
Google may have the ability to spin down its own machine learning workloads as it pleases, but it can't exactly pause its cloud customers' AI jobs without causing a few headaches.
Demand-response isn't the only way Google is looking to curb the power demands of its AI infrastructure build out, and it's not hard to see why. The search giant
plowed
$14 billion into servers in just 91 days of its 2025 fiscal year with plans to spend upwards of $85 billion by year's end.
The company also continues to invest in alternative energy sources, including geothermal, solar, wind, hydroelectric, and nuclear. Google aims to
field
small modular reactors just as soon as they get their hands on one, and in May
signed
an agreement with Elementl Power to support the development of three potential reactor sites in the US. ®

data.title: Show HN: Stagewise (YC S25) – Front end coding agent for existing codebases
data.author: juliangoetze
data.article_summary: Stagewise是首个用于生产级web应用的前端编码代理。它运行于浏览器中，能直接修改本地代码库，支持多种框架和设置。开发者无需繁琐操作，只需通过点击元素和输入指令，即可让stagewise自动完成更改。它提供插件定制功能，并且开源，采用AGPL-3.0许可证。使用时，开发者只需在项目根目录运行指定命令即可启动stagewise，无需额外安装。同时，它支持多种代理工具集成，如Cursor、GitHub Copilot等。社区和支持渠道包括Discord和GitHub issues。

  - dchuk 和 wodow 关心该产品是否能与Ruby on Rails的ERB模板或非JavaScript框架兼容。
  - ProofHouse 则希望支持VanillaJS，以便在更多类型的Web应用中使用。
  - pj_mukh 提到需要支持前端移动开发（React-Native, Swift等），并指出目前类似工具在处理现有代码库上的不足。

• [改进建议] rrrx3 提出希望增加更多设计控制功能，以提升用户体验。

• [市场竞争与合作] chatmasta 提出关于竞争与合作的担忧，询问产品如何在与Webflow、Vercel等公司竞争中建立“护城河”，并建议考虑与这些公司合作，进行白标（white-label）合作。

npx stagewise

pnpm dlx stagewise

data.title: Gate-level emulation of an Intel 4004 in 4004 bytes of C
data.author: mad
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者Nicholas Carlini在国际模糊C代码大赛中的获奖作品：一个用不到4004字节的C语言编写的Intel 4004门级仿真器。该仿真器能够模拟最初为Busicom 141-pf计算器设计的4004芯片。与常规仿真方法不同，作者通过设计一个完整的4004电路（微编码以节省空间），并使用自己开发的miniHDL语言来构建和设计电路。最终，程序将15,000字节的程序和200,000字节的电路压缩至不到4004字节，并在现代计算机上以每秒几百条指令的速度运行，足以实际使用。文章还提到了代码的源码已在GitHub上发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一个4004芯片仿真器的不同看法和技术细节的讨论

不同观点：
• **vrighter的观点**：认为该项目在改变门级电路布局后，不再是对4004芯片的纯粹门级仿真，而是一个通过额外步骤实现的4004仿真器。虽然整个程序作为逻辑仿真器很了不起，但这一点需要指出。

• **kazinator的观点**：提供了一个历史背景，指出4004芯片在Busicom计算器项目中实际上用于解释一个更强大的虚拟机，应用程序的机器代码是针对该虚拟机编写的，而非直接针对4004的指令集，因此Intel并未完全构建一个通用处理器。

• **rep_lodsb的观点**：批评该项目并不是真正仿真4004芯片，而是一个逻辑电路仿真器，通过压缩表示运行并使用I/O机制仿真Busicom计算器硬件。虽然对代码规模印象深刻，但认为“CPU”并不像4004或任何真正的微处理器。

• **dmitrygr的观点**：简单表达了对该项目的欣赏，认为其非常优美，未涉及具体技术细节。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该仿真器是否真正仿真了4004芯片，尤其是门级电路和CPU架构的相似性。
• 讨论中提到了历史背景，即4004在Busicom项目中的实际应用及其虚拟机解释器的角色，这为理解仿真器的性质提供了更多上下文。
• 不同评论者对项目复杂性和技术实现的看法存在差异，有人认为其非常了不起，有人则认为与真实4004有差距。

Main

Writing
Gate-level emulation of an Intel 4004 in 4004 bytes of C
by
Nicholas Carlini
2025-08-04
The International Obfuscated C Code Contest results were announced this last weekend,
and I was thrilled to see that
my entry
was among the winners.
In this article I want to walk through what it is:
a feature-complete gate-level emulator for the Intel 4004 that's capable of emulating the original
Busicom 141-pf calculator ROM---the application for which the 4004 was originally designed.
To make things exciting, this program doesn't emulate the 4004 the "normal" way.
Instead, this program is actually just a logic gate simulator, but where I've designed an entire
4004 as circuit (microcoded for space!) that's embedded in the program and then emulated.
And because we're 50 years in the future, this gate-level emulated calculator
runs at a few hundred instructions per second which
is actually fast enough to be usable, just as long as you're not in a hurry.
This is part two in a two (or maybe three?) part series of posts.
Last time
,
I explained the design of
miniHDL
,
a small python DSL that allows you to build and design circuits.
This time, I'm going to use miniHDL to design my 4004 (along with an intel 4003,
4002, and 4001), and then write some scaffolding so that it has the correct "hardware" to
run the original program ROM,
and then somehow crush a 15,000 byte program and 200,000 byte circuit into the below <4004 bytes.
Source code, as always, is on GitHub.

44799452.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者Nicholas Carlini在国际模糊C代码大赛中的获奖作品：一个用不到4004字节的C语言编写的Intel 4004门级仿真器。该仿真器能够模拟最初为Busicom 141-pf计算器设计的4004芯片。与常规仿真方法不同，作者通过设计一个完整的4004电路（微编码以节省空间），并使用自己开发的miniHDL语言来构建和设计电路。最终，程序将15,000字节的程序和200,000字节的电路压缩至不到4004字节，并在现代计算机上以每秒几百条指令的速度运行，足以实际使用。文章还提到了代码的源码已在GitHub上发布。
44799452.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一个4004芯片仿真器的不同看法和技术细节的讨论

不同观点：
• **vrighter的观点**：认为该项目在改变门级电路布局后，不再是对4004芯片的纯粹门级仿真，而是一个通过额外步骤实现的4004仿真器。虽然整个程序作为逻辑仿真器很了不起，但这一点需要指出。

• **kazinator的观点**：提供了一个历史背景，指出4004芯片在Busicom计算器项目中实际上用于解释一个更强大的虚拟机，应用程序的机器代码是针对该虚拟机编写的，而非直接针对4004的指令集，因此Intel并未完全构建一个通用处理器。

• **rep_lodsb的观点**：批评该项目并不是真正仿真4004芯片，而是一个逻辑电路仿真器，通过压缩表示运行并使用I/O机制仿真Busicom计算器硬件。虽然对代码规模印象深刻，但认为“CPU”并不像4004或任何真正的微处理器。

• **dmitrygr的观点**：简单表达了对该项目的欣赏，认为其非常优美，未涉及具体技术细节。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于该仿真器是否真正仿真了4004芯片，尤其是门级电路和CPU架构的相似性。
• 讨论中提到了历史背景，即4004在Busicom项目中的实际应用及其虚拟机解释器的角色，这为理解仿真器的性质提供了更多上下文。
• 不同评论者对项目复杂性和技术实现的看法存在差异，有人认为其非常了不起，有人则认为与真实4004有差距。

data.title: A new database on police use of force and misconduct in California
data.author: Improvement
data.article_summary: 2025年8月4日，加州推出了一个关于警察使用武力和不当行为的新数据库，公开了150万页曾经保密的警察记录。该数据库由加州大学伯克利分校和斯坦福大学开发，并由《洛杉矶时报》、《旧金山纪事报》、KQED和CalMatters发布。数据库涵盖了近500个执法机构的记录，包括约12,000个案例，其中数千涉及警察枪击事件。这些记录根据加州公共记录法进行了编辑，现在公众可以搜索有关不当行为和使用武力的信息。该数据库名为“警察记录访问项目”，由多学科团队历经多年创建，利用了生成式人工智能等新兴技术。数据库的建立得益于加州最近通过的一系列提高执法透明度的法律，特别是2018年的S.B. 1421和2021年的S.B. 16法案。该数据库将有助于公众、研究人员和警察部门识别趋势、进行招聘决策和推动改革。ACLU和多位立法者参与了项目的推进，认为该数据库对促进执法透明度和问责制至关重要。公众现在可以通过KQED、《旧金山纪事报》、《洛杉矶时报》和CalMatters在线访问该数据库。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：警察改革及相关问题

不同观点：
• **提高警察标准和培训质量**：[altruios] 认为警察应达到最高标准，因为他们拥有合法使用武力的垄断权。他建议结束“有限豁免权”，并引入类似于外科医生的个人保险制度，同时主张延长培训时间、深入学习法律并通过类似律师资格的考试，以确保警察是 exceptional people。他还批评了当前系统倾向于剔除“过于聪明”的人。

• **透明度和数据的作用**：[cadamsdotcom] 强调透明度的双赢作用，认为数据可以帮助识别并清除少数有问题的人员，从而显著提升整体警务质量。他希望通过清除有问题的人员来重建公众信任。

• **内部举报文化**：[zippyman55] 希望警察更愿意举报同事的违规行为，认为目前警队文化倾向于容忍和忽视这些问题。他特别提到不必要的加班费、虚假残疾等问题。

• **对注册制度的担忧**：[nativeit] 支持改革的目标，但对注册制度感到不安，认为这些制度容易被滥用，并常被用来掩盖缺乏实质性改革的事实。他认为机构倾向于牺牲个人以保护整体体制，避免触动现状。

• **警察人员的素质和动机**：[TechDebtDevin] 支持改革，但认为需要不同类型的人来担任警察。他指出许多警察对改革持消极态度，甚至停止执行任务，并提到其城市警察将问题归咎于民主党的市长。

• **对加州警察的讽刺**：[Simon_O_Rourke] 以讽刺的口吻评论加州警察总是把问题搞得更糟，虽然没有提出具体建议或解决方案，但表达了对现状的不满。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：不同观点之间的争议主要集中在如何有效实现警察改革。一方面，有人主张通过提高标准和培训质量来改善警察队伍；另一方面，有人担心这些措施可能被系统滥用或导致警察消极怠工。此外，对注册制度的有效性和透明度措施的实际效果也存在不同看法。

• **共同关注点**：所有评论者都表达了对当前警察系统某些方面的不满，并同意需要进行某种形式的改革，以提高警察的专业水平和公众信任。

• **文化问题**：评论中多次提到警队内部文化的问题，特别是对举报同事违规行为的容忍度和对问题人员的处理。这被认为是改革过程中需要解决的重要方面。

A new database on police use of force and misconduct in California makes public 1.5 million pages of once-secret police records
August 4, 2025
For Immediate Release
August 4, 2025
Contact: Journalism@berkeley.edu
A new database on police use of force and misconduct in California makes public 1.5 million pages of once-secret police records
Public records about use of force and misconduct by California law enforcement officers — some 1.5 million pages obtained from nearly 500 law enforcement agencies — will now be searchable by the public for the first time thanks to a new database built by UC Berkeley and Stanford University and published today by the
Los Angeles Times
,
San Francisco Chronicle
,
KQED
and
CalMatters
.
The database — the first of its kind in the nation — will vastly expand public access to internal affairs records that disclose how law enforcement agencies throughout the state h
andle misconduct allegations as well as uses of police force that result in death or serious injury. The database, funded by the State of California, currently has records from nearly 12,000 cases, including thousands involving police shootings. Every record in the database was released by a law enforcement agency after being redacted in compliance with California’s public records laws. As a result, journalists and members of the public will now be able to
search statewide for particular types of misconduct and use-of-force. Police chiefs will be able to use the data to aid in hiring decisions. Researchers will be able to identify trends and patterns.
The database, called the Police Records Access Project, is the product of years of work by a multidisciplinary team of journalists, data scientists, lawyers and civil liberties advocates, led by UC Berkeley Journalism’s
Investigative Reporting Program
(IRP)
,
the
Berkeley Institute for Data Science
(BIDS), and Stanford University’s
Big Local News
. Other key contributors include the
ACLU Foundation of Southern California
, California innocence organizations, the
National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers
, UC Irvine law school’s
Press Freedom Project
and UC Berkeley law school’s
Criminal Law & Justice Center
.
The team systematically collected, organized and vetted millions of public records, used emerging technologies such as generative AI to build the database, and created from scratch a searchable user-interface.
“The creation of a public facing database is critical for all of the stakeholders in the criminal legal system: whether public defenders, innocence organizations, prosecutors, police departments or academics,” said Barry Scheck, co-founder and special counsel to the Innocence Project. “This information can be used to understand the system and reform it.”
Aditya Parameswaran, an associate professor at
UC Berkeley’s Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences,
led work on the database at BIDS. “Here we have an amazing example of how generative AI
— with humans in the loop —
can be used for good, at a scale that’s unprecedented, for a task that’s never been done before and for societal impact,” he said.
Creation of the database was made possible by a series of landmark laws adopted recently by the state of California to improve transparency around law enforcement. Through
S.B. 1421
, approved in 2018, and
S.B. 16
, approved in 2021, California made records related to uses of force and misconduct accessible to the public for the first time. However, requesting these documents through the Public Records Act required going agency by agency, a laborious process that has made it impossible until now to identify trends and patterns across the state.
“For 40 years California hid police misconduct,’’ said former state Sen. Nancy Skinner, who helped lead the legislative push for the new transparency laws and played a key role in securing state funding to create the database. “We were able to open those records to the public when the legislature passed S.B. 1421 in 2019. Now with this new database, Californians will have even better access, making it easier to find out which law enforcement officers have a history of bad behavior and which of our police departments do the right thing to hold their officers accountable.’’
Tiffany Bailey, senior staff attorney at the ACLU Foundation of Southern California, which will contribute an additional 200,000 records to the database from its own efforts to obtain police records under S.B. 1421, said the Police Records Access Project will be a “vital tool’’ in holding law enforcement agencies accountable. “Critically, families who have lost loved ones in California will now have direct access to the information they need to seek meaningful accountability that has too often been denied,” Bailey said.
The database released today can now be accessed online via KQED, The San Francisco Chronicle, Los Angeles Times and CalMatters. The database does not include audio recordings or videos, and additional s
